BETA Close X Card Factory PLC has announced the purchase of 1,089,912 of its own ordinary shares between May 25th and May 29th, 2026, at prices ranging from 67.00 pence to 74.00 pence per share, with a volume-weighted average price of approximately 70.99 pence. These repurchased shares will be cancelled, reducing the total number of issued ordinary shares to 347,789,223. The company currently holds 4,219,673 ordinary shares in treasury. Disclaimer* Card Factory PLC 01 June 2026 1 June 2026 'Card Factory plc (the "Company") Transactions in own shares Card Factory plc, the UK's leading specialist retailer of greeting cards, gifts and celebration essentials, announces that it purchased the following number of ordinary shares of 1 pence each in the capital of the Company ('Ordinary Shares') through UBS AG London Branch. The Ordinary Shares purchased will be cancelled. Date of purchase: 25 May 2026 26 May 2026 27 May 2026 28 May 2026 29 May 2026 Number of ordinary shares purchased: 0 219,932 181,734 346,015 105,301 Highest price paid per share (pence per share): 0.00 72.80 74.00 70.40 69.00 Lowest price paid per share (pence per share): 0.00 71.40 72.30 67.40 67.00 Volume weighted average price paid per share (pence per share): 0.0000 72.2260 73.5276 68.2941 67.5924 The Company notifies the market that at the date of this announcement the Company's issued ordinary share capital comprises 348,879,135 ordinary shares with a nominal value of 1p each ("Ordinary Shares") with each share carrying one vote. In aggregate, 4,219,673 Ordinary Shares are held in treasury. The number of 344,659,462 ordinary shares may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change in their interest in, the ordinary share capital of the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules. This disclosure is made pursuant to paragraph 9.6.6(R) of the Listing Rules. The table below contains detailed information about the purchases made as part of the Share repurchase programme.
